title: A Stacks-defined left derived value is a pointwise Kan-extension value
statement: Let $D$ and $D'$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], let $S$ be a saturated multiplicative system in $D$ compatible with the triangulated structure, let $Q:D\to S^{-1}D$ be its localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $F:D\to D'$ be exact. Let $X$ be an object of $D$ and $Y$ an object of $D'$. If the left derived functor of $F$ is defined at $X$ in the sense of Stacks Definition Tag 05S9 with value $Y$ (the pro-object $(S/X)\to D'$, $(s:X'\to X)\mapsto F(X')$, is essentially constant with value $Y$), then $F$ has a pointwise right Kan extension along $Q$ at $QX$ with value $Y$: the limit of $F$ over the structured-arrow category of pairs $(X',\ QX\to QX')$ exists and is $Y$. Moreover the limit projection at $(X,\mathrm{id}_{QX})$, the comparison map $Y\to F(X)$, is the canonical map of Definition 05S9.
